checkpoints: Concatenating `pushedTimeline` and `celebrityPosts` without deduplicating by `id` breaks the moment an author is promoted from regular to KOL: both queries filter on the author's *current* celebrity flag rather than the flag at the time each post was written, so an author's older posts still sit in the push path while the same posts are now also pulled into the celebrity path, and every one of them renders twice in the merged feed.

The correct fix is a dedup pass keyed on `post.id` — for example building a `Map<string, Post>` or a `Set<string>` of seen ids while iterating the merged array and keeping only the first occurrence — applied right before the sort, not a change to either source query, since each query is individually correct and it is only the union that is wrong.

Because `this.getSaltedKolKey('kol_1', userId)` always passes the literal string `'kol_1'` instead of the celebrity's real `authorId`, every celebrity's cache is written and read under the exact same key family regardless of how many distinct KOLs exist in `celebrityIds`; once there is more than one celebrity, one celebrity's cache read can silently return another celebrity's cached timeline.

The fix for the salted-key bug is to pass the actual celebrity `authorId` being cached into `getSaltedKolKey` instead of a fixture id, and if the intent is one cache entry per KOL rather than one blended cache per reading user, cache each celebrity's timeline separately under its own real `authorId` and merge the cached results at read time instead of blending first and caching once under a shared identity.

Both the missing dedup and the hardcoded salted key are correctness bugs — the user is shown a wrong or cross-contaminated feed, not just a slow one — so they belong ahead of any cosmetic or stylistic PR comments and should be raised as blockers rather than nitpicks.

The tests passing and the demo timeline looking right prove nothing about the promotion case, since a single-snapshot dataset where no author's celebrity flag has ever changed can never exercise the stale-row overlap that causes the duplicate; the review has to explicitly reason about what happens the day an author crosses the threshold, not just about the code's current behavior.

A related but independent gap worth flagging is that nothing TTLs or deletes an author's stale push-timeline rows once they are promoted to celebrity, so even after the dedup fix lands, the duplicate-post problem keeps compounding on every future read unless a cleanup job or expiry handles the role-drift cleanup.

Concrete verification for these bugs means seeding an author as a regular user with existing posts, promoting them to celebrity, calling the hybrid feed, and asserting every `post.id` appears exactly once in the timeline; and separately seeding two distinct celebrities and asserting `getSaltedKolKey` resolves to two different keys rather than one shared key.
